title: runtime/scheduler: add request classification module (short vs long) w/ conservative defaults
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype needs a stable, conservative way to split requests into prefill-heavy vs interactive so we can isolate tail latency from long-context traffic without impacting overall throughput.

This PR introduces a request classification module in the runtime scheduler layer.

What it does: Adds a small `RequestClassifier` that computes a `WorkClass` for each incoming request (SHORT | LONG) based on prompt-length thresholds and an explicit prefill-cost estimate. The prefill-cost estimate is intentionally a stub for now (derived from token counts + model config constants) so we can land the plumbing + tests and then iterate on accuracy (EWMA/observed timings) without reshaping the scheduler APIs.

Classification inputs (current): (1) prompt token count (preferred) or prompt char length (fallback if tokenization metadata absent), (2) max_new_tokens / expected decode budget, (3) optional client hint (tier/latency_sensitive) carried through request metadata, (4) model context window + known prefill slope constants.

Policy (conservative defaults): Default-to-LONG when metadata is missing/ambiguous (e.g., unknown token count, failed tokenization, or prompt too close to threshold). Only classify as SHORT when we are confident the request is not prefill-heavy. This minimizes the risk of a misclassified long prompt entering the short queue and inflating p95.

Knobs (config only, no API changes): (a) `scheduler.classifier.short_prompt_tokens_max` (default 256), (b) `scheduler.classifier.long_prompt_tokens_min` (default 512), (c) `scheduler.classifier.prefill_cost_short_ms_max` (default 22ms on A100; scaled by model profile), (d) `scheduler.classifier.enable_client_hints` (default false). Threshold gap (hysteresis) is intentional to reduce oscillation around boundaries.

Tests: Adds unit tests for threshold boundaries, missing metadata fallback, hysteresis behavior, and override semantics (client hint cannot force SHORT if prompt is clearly long; can force LONG if latency-insensitive batch job).

Non-goals: No queueing/dispatch changes here (that’s ENG-4823). No real prefill predictor yet (stub only). No metrics yet (ENG-4824 will handle per-class queue depth + wait histograms).

Rollout/compat: Module is internal-only and not wired to dispatch in this PR; it is safe to land ahead of the feature-flagged scheduler policy.

Changed areas (high level): - runtime/scheduler: new classifier implementation + integration point in request ingest path (not used for dispatch yet) - runtime/proto: add internal enum for `WorkClass` (SHORT/LONG/UNKNOWN) - tests: new classifier test suite and table-driven cases

Files (not exhaustive): - runtime/scheduler/classification/request_classifier.h - runtime/scheduler/classification/request_classifier.cc - runtime/scheduler/classification/work_class.h - runtime/scheduler/request_context.h (plumbs prompt token count if present) - runtime/config/runtime_config.schema.json (internal knobs) - runtime/scheduler/classification/request_classifier_test.cc

Illustrative snippet: `if (prompt_tokens == nullopt) return WorkClass::LONG; // safe default` and `if (prompt_tokens <= short_prompt_tokens_max && estimated_prefill_ms <= prefill_cost_short_ms_max) return WorkClass::SHORT;`

Follow-ups: (1) add observed-prefill EWMA to estimator behind guardrails (tracked in ENG-4830/ENG-4831), (2) hook class into two-queue scheduler flag (ENG-4823), (3) metrics + sampled logs (ENG-4824).

Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you clarify why default-to-LONG is preferred vs UNKNOWN? We might want UNKNOWN to keep current behavior.

Marcus Reed (author): Good point. I used LONG because the next PR (two-queue) will treat LONG as the safe lane; UNKNOWN would require a third path. For this PR, I can rename the internal enum to include UNKNOWN but keep default mapping to LONG until we actually have a 3-way behavior.

Lena Fischer (review): Threshold hysteresis looks good, but the gap (256/512) feels wide. Did we base this on any distribution?

Marcus Reed (author): No hard data yet; chosen to avoid oscillation and to ensure the SHORT class is truly short. Once we run trace replays we can tune. I’ll add comments noting these are intentionally conservative and expected to be tuned.

Omar El-Sayed (review): The prefill estimator stub uses model_profile.prefill_ms_per_token. Where does that come from, and what’s the unit? Also please ensure we don’t accidentally treat it as authoritative in future.

Marcus Reed (author): Comes from the existing model performance profile used by batching heuristics; unit is ms/token. I added `// stub` comments + a TODO pointing to EWMA replacement. Also added a clamp to avoid weird profiles producing negative/zero.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Please ensure classifier doesn’t influence kernel selection or batch formation in this PR.

Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed: classification is computed and attached to RequestContext only; no dispatch/kernel path reads it yet. Added a regression test that ensures scheduler chooses same execution path with classifier enabled/disabled.

Marcus Reed (author): Added both cases + a small helper for prompt_tokens-only workloads.
